caption:
Etsy is banning AI-generated recipes, patterns and instructions, plus listings made by bots with no human involvement.
Most listings now need at least one unedited photo of the real item. Pattern sellers must show a finished piece someone actually made.
AI art can stay if the seller discloses it and plays a clear creative role.

Have you ever bought something online that turned out to be AI?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Value Added Resource
threads_text: Etsy just banned AI-generated recipes and crochet patterns, and most listings now need one unedited photo of the real item. Etsy says buyers can't tell what's AI anymore, and it's keeping them from shopping. Should every marketplace do this?

site_article.summary: Etsy announced on October 22, 2026, that sellers can no longer offer AI-generated patterns, recipes and other functional guides, and that most listings must include at least one unedited photo of the real item. AI-generated art remains allowed when sellers play a clear creative role and disclose it.
site_article.seo_title: Etsy bans AI-generated recipes and patterns, adds photo rule
site_article.seo_description: Etsy now bans AI-generated patterns, recipes and bot-made listings, and most listings need one unedited photo of the actual item.
site_article.answer_summary: Etsy no longer allows sellers to list AI-generated patterns, recipes, instructions or other functional guides, or listings made by bots without human involvement. AI art is still permitted with disclosure.

paragraphs.text: Etsy announced on October 22, 2026, that sellers may no longer sell AI-generated functional guides on the marketplace. According to Value Added Resource, the ban covers knitting, crochet, sewing, embroidery, quilting and beading patterns, recipes, woodworking and construction plans, instruction manuals and other task guides. Traders Union, citing CNBC, reported the same change.

Etsy also prohibited fully automated listings, meaning content generated by bots or products and listings created in bulk without individual human creative input and oversight. Value Added Resource noted that AI prompt bundles were already prohibited under a 2024 rule.
A real photo on most listings

Most listings must now include at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background. Value Added Resource reported that this image cannot be cropped, resized, straightened or adjusted for lighting or exposure, and its background cannot be changed. Sellers of craft patterns, recipes, seeds and similar products must show at least one real photo of a finished result made or grown with the product, so a crochet pattern listing has to show a completed project rather than an AI image of how it should look.

Edits are still allowed on additional listing images, including cropping, color changes and AI-based edits, as long as the images represent the item accurately. Print on demand sellers who use production partners for standard products such as t-shirts or mugs may use authorized stock mockups, according to Value Added Resource.

Etsy is not removing AI art. AI-generated artwork remains permitted when the seller plays a clear creative role, discloses the use of AI and does not present the work as handmade or entirely their own creation, according to Traders Union and NewsBytes.

Etsy said many active buyers report that they cannot tell which items involve AI content, and that this is one of the top three barriers to shopping on the platform more often. Value Added Resource reported that the changes follow seller criticism of AI-generated crochet patterns during a November 2025 Ask Me Anything event with chief executive Kruti Patel Goyal.

Misleading listings can be removed, and repeat violations can lead to the removal of a shop. Sellers may have to refund buyers who open cases over items that are materially different from their listings. Etsy will notify sellers in the listing form when it detects AI-generated images at upload, plans to extend detection to existing listings and is adding a way for members to flag misleading AI imagery. At first, those reports will be used to gather information rather than to trigger enforcement. Value Added Resource reported that the announcement did not set a deadline for existing listings to comply.

The policy draws a line between AI used as a creative tool and AI used to produce instructions that buyers rely on to make something. For a marketplace built on handmade goods, buyer trust is the core product, and the photo rule shifts the burden of proof onto sellers.

The next thing to watch is how Etsy enforces the rule on existing listings, including whether it sets a compliance deadline and how its upload detection separates banned AI content from permitted edits.
